title: Rotate Image
contract: Rotate an n×n matrix clockwise by 90 degrees.
brute: int n=a.length;int[][] out=new int[n][n];for(int r=0;r<n;r++)for(int c=0;c<n;c++){out[c][n-1-r]=a[r][c];emit("Map a cell to its rotated coordinates","source",new int[]{r,c},"output",out);}return out;
optimal: int n=a.length;for(int r=0;r<n;r++)for(int c=r+1;c<n;c++){int t=a[r][c];a[r][c]=a[c][r];a[c][r]=t;}emit("Transpose across the main diagonal","matrix",a);for(int[] row:a){for(int l=0,r=n-1;l<r;l++,r--){int t=row[l];row[l]=row[r];row[r]=t;}emit("Reverse each transposed row","matrix",a);}return a;
reasoning: Map each original (r,c) to (c,n−1−r) in a new matrix.
Clockwise rotation equals transpose followed by reversing each row.
Swap only above the diagonal while transposing, otherwise each pair is swapped twice. In-place rotation requires a square matrix; rectangular rotation needs different dimensions.
